description.narrative: The objective of the Expanding Opportunities for Learning Project in Djibouti is to increase equitable access to basic education, improve teaching practices, and strengthen Ministry of National Education and Vocational Training (MENFOP) management capacity. This project consists of four components. Component 1: Establishing foundations for quality preschool education. The main objectives of this component are to establish quality standards for preschool education and to improve preschool classroom pedagogy. Sub-component 1.1: Improving the quality of and access to preschool education. Sub-component 1.2: Results-based financing for strengthening preschool quality. Component 2: Expanding access to and improving retention in primary and lower secondary education. Sub-component 2.1: Expanding access to primary and lower secondary education and improving retention of vulnerable and underserved groups. Sub-component 2.2: Results based financing for expanding access and improving retention in primary and lower secondary education. Component 3: Building capacity to support teaching and learning. Sub-component 3.1: Improving the quality of learning assessments, professional development, and pedagogical resources. Sub-component 3.2: Results-based financing for improvements in learning assessments and professional development. Component 4: Strengthening MENFOP's management capacity and data systems. Sub-component 4.1: Modernization of the education management information systems and sub-component 4.2: Support to project management and M&E.
The project development objective is to increase equitable access to basic education, improve teaching practices, and strengthen MENFOP's management capacity.

title.narrative: PDO #4: Learning assessments are revised and administered

target.value: Revised OTIs (years 2 and 5) and at least one national learning assessment are administered

comment.narrative: The grade 2 OTI (Objectifs Terminaux d’Intégration) have been revised and approved. In line with international best practices, grade 2 primary school OTIs have been transformed into continuous assessments which have been implemented since the school year 2021-22. The Grade 5 OTI has been revised following the roll-out of the revised curriculum in school year 2023-24.nbsp; National Assessments of Learning (ENI) have been introduced for Grade 2 and will provide an alternative assessment to the OTI final test at the end of the second year. An Early Grade Reading Assessment (EGRA) was administered in the 2020-21 school year with support from USAID. A first independent national assessment in literacy and numeracy for grade 2 was administered an piloted in April/May 2022, a second national assessment of a representative sample for Grade 2 was administered in 2022/23. A follow up national assessment for Grade 2 is being administered for school year 2023-24 together with the first administration of a national assessment for Grade 4. MENFOP has become a member of an international learning assessment through PASEC (Programme d'analyse des systems éducatifs de la CONFEMEN-pays francophone) which will allow Djibouti to be comparatively assessed against other countries for the first time.

target.value: Revised OTIs (years 2 and 5) and at least one national learning assessment are administered

comment.narrative: The grade 2 OTI (Objectifs Terminaux dâ€™IntAgration)Â have been revised and approved. In line with international best practices, grade 2 primary school OTIs have been transformed into continuous assessments which have been implemented since the school year 2021-22. The Grade 5 OTI has beenÂ revised following the roll-out of the revised curriculum in school year 2023-24.Â National Assessments of Learning (ENI)Â have been introduced for Grade 2 and will provide an alternative assessment to the OTI final test at the end of the second year.Â An Early Grade Reading Assessment (EGRA) was administered in the 2020-21 school year with support from USAID. A firstÂ independent national assessment in literacy and numeracy for grade 2 was administered and piloted in April/May 2022,Â and a second national assessmentÂ of a representative sample for Grade 2 was administered in 2022/23.Â A follow-up national assessment for Grade 2 was administered for the school year 2023-24 together with Grade 4.

comment.narrative: GOSE has been extended to middle and high school students since the last mission. In addition, the information system is now able to manage absences (among other things, it can automatically send SMS messages to parents of absent pupils) and pupils' results (creation of report cards after class councils). A school infrastructure module is currently under development. In the future, it is planned that the platform will include private schools and schools for EABS, that it will be open to parents, that it will become the basis for the statistical yearbook, and that it will enable certain analyses (e.g. on the impact of pre-school on learning).

comment.narrative: Indicator achieved. Following the revision of the grade 9 curriculum, the Brevet des collèges has been updated. Previously, all subjects were tested in paper-based exams. This number has now been reduced, to focus on the main subjects (math, French, science). The other subjects are tested in continuous assessment. The first administration of the revised brevet took place in May 2024.
